body:
So I looked into it a bit. I'd prefer not to include CC-BY-SA code if we can avoid it, because:
- It's the first occurrence of this license so we'd need to add it in full in COPYRIGHT.txt :stuck_out_tongue: 
- It's an unconventional license for code, and some folks might be worried about the ShareAlike clause (I believe it only applies if you modify this code and re-share it, but some might see it as a stronger copyleft that forces sharing modifications).

But looking at the code in the StackOverflow comment, I'm not sure we should treat this as thirdparty/copyrighted in the first place.

The coefficients seem to be the ones documented here: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YCbCr#Approximate_8-bit_matrices_for_BT.601
And so it's a pretty basic transformation that I don't think warrants attribution or copyright.

So I'd suggest moving this code to `modules/theora` and make it fully part of the Godot first-party code.
Can still link to the stackoverflow (and maybe wikipedia page) for reference.

The way it is now already implies that the user knows that the OGV format has to be selected via the file extension for those settings to work, and then an error will be shown for the unsupported formats. This project settings section could be better improved in other ways IMHO.
I'd say it can be bound in register types as long as it's bound before the class itself is registered, that's probably why this happens
